newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures close pit trading weaker.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures close pit trading weaker.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures whittled losses into the close but still finished pit trading weaker.

Afternoon trade had slowed markedly from a brisk morning pace, with turnover dominated by cross action as players began buying back marks against other units, including Swiss francs, Japanese yen and sterling.

"Everything's really just spread-related. It's the first time in days the Swiss has been lower than the mark," said one floor broker at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange. "Everything is headline-reacting and cross-reacting."
Comments by Federal Reserve vice chairman Alice Rivlin also briefly tugged currencies upward, especially the mark, after she said the dollar may not get much stronger.

She also told the House Banking committee it was a "tough call" to decide whether the Fed needed to raise rates further. She said there seems to be little risk of the U.S. economy moving into recession and that risks of inflation seem higher.

Currencies showed little response to the second day of Humphrey-Hawkins testimony by Fed chairman Alan Greenspan. Nor did they react much to remarks by Fed governor Laurence Meyer and New York Fed president William McDonough.

Traders noted good activity during the morning, when one firm was seen covering up to 4,000 September marks and 2,000 yen and selling roughly 500 sterling. Some brokers said the activity looked like spread unwinding.

September pounds jumped early on a bigger than expected 0.6 percent in June in U.K. retail sales from May but then broke back down on cross activity and as traders debated how to interpret comments by Bank of England Governor Eddie George.
George said some of sterling's rise was irrational and that Britain's new monetary policy committee carried no bias on interest rates one way or another.
Some traders said George's remarks hinted at the possibility that U.K. rates might not rise again soon.
Sterling's ensuing swings also pounded traders, they said.
"The pound broke down and came back and whipsawed the hell out of a whole lot of folks," said a floor bank broker.

At settlement, Sept yen lost $0.000028 to $0.008713, marks eased $0.0008 to $0.5494, Swiss francs lost $0.0017 to $0.6771, stlering dipped $0.0004 to $1.6754, Can dollar lost $0.0023 to $0.7263, Aussie dollar dropped $0.0028 to $0.7372, and Mexican peso rose $0.000050 to $0.125000.
